events.did: Checked the tag on a pair of white sneakers in a downtown Portsmith shoe store and found they cost two hundred bucks
events.quote_anchor: He looked down, admiring the pristine white of the sneakers before he checked the tag. Two hundred bucks.

events.did: Snapped the tag off the sneakers and tucked it into the box while the clerk was in the back
events.quote_anchor: As soon as he was out of sight, Xavi snapped the tag, and tucked it into the box, strolling toward the exit.

events.did: Touched the clerk's hand where it gripped his coat, so the clerk's mind rewound and the whole store interaction was erased
events.quote_anchor: And then the clerk’s mind was zipping backward, the whole brief interaction in the store rewound, unraveled, erased.

events.did: Rewound the whole shared history of the girl who clerked in the shop where he bought his new windbreaker
events.quote_anchor: The clerk was a girl who’d known him back in middle school, and he’d ended up rewinding their whole shared history, just to be safe.

events.did: Beat the level of the Memory game and took two dozen tickets
events.quote_anchor: He beat the level and the game spit out two dozen tickets.

events.who: the man in black motorcycle gear
events.did: Walked toward Xavi drawing a weapon, a cattle prod whose tip sparked blue
events.quote_anchor: He started walking toward Xavi, drawing a weapon as he did. A cattle prod, the tip sparking blue.

events.did: Wrenched the metal door back open to run through the arcade and found a second stranger in the same black gear
events.quote_anchor: He spun and wrenched the metal door back open, intending to cut through the arcade, but instead he found a second stranger in the same black gear.

events.did: Was punched in the chest by a dart between his ribs and began falling without ever hitting the ground
events.quote_anchor: Xavi staggered and looked down, saw a dart jutting between his ribs, pain and numbness rushing in its wake.

relations.did: Works for Victor Vale, who hired him and warns him about a shadowy organization that captures people like them
relations.quote_anchor: Going on about some shadowy organization designed to find and capture people like them. Victor was obviously paranoid. Hell, that was why he’d hired Xavi.

relations.did: Took a liking to Xavi and said they could be friends
relations.quote_anchor: but she took a liking to him, said they could be friends (hell, he’d just been stoked to know there were others out there like him).

relations.did: Passed Xavi's name to Victor, who gave him the job
relations.quote_anchor: And then she’d passed his name to Victor, who gave him the job, and it had all been up, up, up since then.

relations.did: Is one of the Pascals; his dad said the Pascals were survivors and his aunt said they only looked out for themselves
relations.quote_anchor: His dad used to say he’d land on his feet because the Pascals were survivors. His aunt, well, she said that was because they only looked out for themselves.

numbers.quote_anchor: He looked down, admiring the pristine white of the sneakers before he checked the tag. Two hundred bucks.
The clerk sighed even though the store was empty. Ten minutes till close.

numbers.did: asked to see the sneakers in a twelve
numbers.quote_anchor: “These are great,” he said. “But can I see them in a twelve?”

numbers.did: ran ten symbols long, then fifteen, then twenty
numbers.quote_anchor: Xavi jabbed the buttons on the game, copying the sequence as it flashed across the screen. Ten symbols long, then fifteen, then twenty.

numbers.did: won two dozen tickets from the Memory game
numbers.quote_anchor: He beat the level and the game spit out two dozen tickets.

numbers.did: was sixteen, too old for the system and too young to get by on his own
numbers.quote_anchor: At sixteen, he was too old for the system, and too young to get by on his own.
